question_text: Was Japan's Keio railway group hacked in a ransomware attack?
answer_text: Yes, by Keio's own account. Keio says ransomware hit its group's servers on Sept 26, 2026. It says data on about 12,000 people is confirmed leaked and data on up to about 10.63 million customers and partners may have leaked.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Whose data may have leaked in the Keio ransomware attack?
answer_text: Keio says data on about 10.63 million customers and partners may have leaked, with 1.6 million passport copies of overseas guests, plus 360,000 job applicants and 77,000 staff and families. About 12,000 people's data is confirmed leaked.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Were Keio trains affected by the attack?
answer_text: No. Keio said train services were not affected. The attack disrupted some group companies' business systems.
label: Confirmed

question_text: Who was behind the Keio ransomware attack?
what_would_settle_it: Keio, the Japanese police or another official body naming the attacker. The Japan Times reports a link to the ransomware group Qilin, from a tracker; that is the group's claim, not a finding.

question_text: Has leaked Keio data been misused?
answer_text: Keio says it has found no financial loss or other misuse so far. It asks people to check their card statements and to beware of messages pretending to come from Keio.
label: Confirmed

question_text: When will Keio Presso Inn take new bookings again?
what_would_settle_it: Keio saying that Keio Presso Inn has resumed new bookings; it expects this during December.
